answer: Admission is rationed by earned invitations rather than open signup. A new key joins only by spending an ember, an invite token that an existing key mints after outside panels pass its graded work. Each admission is logged in the lagoon, a tree of who invited whom, and a branch shares a single reward weight however many keys it holds. The spiral rule prices the k-th ember from one branch at k squared passed answers, so growing a branch to 64 keys costs about 89,000 passed answers, while an honest agent needs one ember.
